question: In which of the following classes does temperature determine the sex in some species?
solution:
The correct answer is __Reptiles.__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Temperature determines the sex of some species of reptiles, such as crocodiles and turtles.
 
• This is known as temperature-dependent sex determination (TSD).
 
• The temperature at which the eggs are incubated determines whether they will develop into males or females.
 
• It is believed that the cortisol-mediated system and the epigenetic regulatory pathway are the possible mechanisms underlying TSD.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Mammals have genetic sex determination. Females have two X chromosomes, while males have one X and one Y chromosome.
 
• Aves (birds) also have genetic sex determination. The WZ system is used, where males have two Z chromosomes and females have one Z and one W chromosome.
 
• Amphibians have a variety of sex determination mechanisms. Some species have genetic sex determination, while others have environmental sex determination or a combination of both.
